Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual WYO filing-determination cycle — decides which FEMA and state actions (Arrangement re-subscription, TRRP re-certification, Flood Insurance Manual adoption, any state informational SFIP filing) are triggered for the coming plan year; escalates open questions to Regulatory Counsel.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 44 CFR 62.23(a) and the current-FY WYO Financial Assistance/Subsidy Arrangement as published in the Federal Register (rep: FY2027 Arrangement, 90 FR, 2026-08728), re-read at the start of every determination cycle since the Arrangement is republished each FEMA fiscal year

In-scope processes.value: Annual WYO plan-year onboarding — from the Federal Register publication of the new Arrangement through the internal determination of every FEMA and state action required to keep NFIP flood-writing authority active for the coming plan year

In-scope systems.value: Internal Regulatory System tracks the FEMA Arrangement cycle, TRRP status and Flood Insurance Manual edition in force; Regulatory Filing Portal (SERFF) is checked for any state informational filing an SFIP form/rate change would trigger

Compliance procedure documented.value: WYO Annual Filing Determination Procedure — Federal Register monitoring, Arrangement redline, TRRP re-certification scoping, Flood Insurance Manual change scoping, state informational-filing scoping, and sign-off routing

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance; reviewed each FEMA fiscal year before the new Arrangement is published and on any mid-year FEMA bulletin

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: The Arrangement must be executed and returned to FEMA at least six months before the plan-year effective date; the determination must close early enough to leave that six-month window intact

Deadline reminders configured.value: Internal Regulatory System calendar alerts at T-9/T-7/T-6 months against the plan-year effective date, escalating to Head of Compliance if the six-month window is at risk

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Determination worksheet, dated Federal Register capture of the current Arrangement, and the prior-year Arrangement redline retained 5 years, consistent with FEMA OIG/NFIP BSA audit look-back

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any plan year entered without a completed, signed-off determination is logged as an exception with root cause, the FEMA action missed, and a remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Compliance Officer signs off every determination and every late or missed re-subscription remediation before the plan year effective date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every FEMA fiscal-year WYO Arrangement cycle plus every SFIP form/rate/rule bulletin FEMA issued in the period, drawn from the Federal Register tracking log and the FEMA WYO bulletin distribution list

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — the Arrangement must be signed and returned before the six-month deadline; a missed deadline is an automatic fail regardless of eventual cure

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Annual test aligned to the FEMA fiscal-year Arrangement cycle, supplemented by an ad hoc test whenever FEMA issues a mid-year Flood Insurance Manual or form bulletin

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared the determination worksheet being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual WYO filing-determination test workpaper filed in the compliance evidence repository under the FEMA fiscal year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Executed Arrangement, determination log extract and dated Federal Register capture, presentable to FEMA/NFIP BSA within 5 business days of a program review request

checklist.step: Monitor the Federal Register for the new FY WYO Arrangement
actions: Maintain a Federal Register saved search for 'WYO Financial Assistance/Subsidy Arrangement' and 'National Flood Insurance Program' notices.
On publication, download the new Arrangement PDF, note its Federal Register citation (e.g. 90 FR, docket number) and publication date.
Log the plan-year effective date and confirm the publication date leaves at least six months before that date.
Create the FY entry in Internal Regulatory System with the citation, publication date and computed six-month deadline.
checklist.done: the current FY Arrangement is captured with its Federal Register citation and the six-month deadline is logged.

checklist.step: Redline the new Arrangement against the prior FY version
actions: Pull the prior FY's executed Arrangement from the compliance evidence repository.
Run a clause-by-clause redline against the new FY text in Microsoft Excel or a document comparison tool.
Flag every changed article, especially reimbursement (Art. III.C), TRRP requirements, and underwriting/claims conformance clauses.
Route any substantive change to Regulatory Counsel for a read before proceeding.
checklist.done: a redline exists identifying every changed clause and Regulatory Counsel has reviewed substantive changes.

checklist.step: Confirm the current Flood Insurance Manual edition and its effective date
actions: Check FEMA's NFIP Flood Insurance Manual distribution for the edition effective for the coming period (manual updates typically take effect April 1).
Compare the new edition's transmittal/change pages to the edition currently loaded in the rating engine.
List every rating factor, form or underwriting-rule change on the determination worksheet with its manual page reference.
Notify the Policy Administration Analyst of the list so a system-change ticket can be scoped.
checklist.done: the current Manual edition, its effective date, and every changed page are logged on the worksheet.

checklist.step: Determine whether TRRP re-certification is required this cycle
actions: Check whether any Transaction Record Reporting and Processing (TRRP) Plan D layout change was published with the new Manual or Arrangement.
Confirm with the Regulatory Reporting Analyst whether the current TRRP certification remains valid or a new test-tape cycle is required.
Record the determination (re-certification required / not required) with its basis on the worksheet.
checklist.done: the worksheet states whether TRRP re-certification is required and why.

checklist.step: Scope any state informational filing triggered by the change
actions: For each writing state, check in SERFF Filing Rules whether the state requires an informational filing acknowledging the current SFIP/Homeowner Flood Form edition or Manual rating basis.
Note in the worksheet, per state, whether an informational filing is required, exempt (federally-prescribed form), or already on file from a prior cycle.
Flag states with an affirmative informational-filing requirement for the Regulatory Filing Specialist to prepare.
checklist.done: every writing state has a recorded informational-filing determination with its SERFF basis.

checklist.step: Confirm community participation status has not lapsed for any writing community
actions: Pull the current book of in-force NFIP policies by community number.
Cross-check each community against FEMA's Community Status Book / Community Information System for suspension or probation status.
Flag any community showing suspended or probationary status for immediate escalation to Compliance Officer — new business there must stop.
checklist.done: every writing community's participation status is confirmed current, with any suspensions flagged and escalated.

checklist.step: Classify each identified item as FEMA filing, TRRP action, state informational filing, or system-only change
actions: On the determination worksheet, tag each row ARRANGEMENT, TRRP, STATE-INFORMATIONAL, MANUAL-SYSTEM or NON-FILED.
For each tag, name the accountable performer (Regulatory Filing Specialist for FEMA/state submissions, Policy Administration Analyst for system-only changes).
Confirm no row is left untagged before moving to package preparation.
checklist.done: every worksheet row carries a tag and a named accountable performer.

checklist.step: Support every 'no action required' call with a named basis
actions: For each NON-FILED row, name the basis (form/rate is federally prescribed with no company discretion; state exempts NFIP filings under its own bulletin; item is a prior-cycle carryover already on file).
Paste the citation or state bulletin reference supporting the basis.
Never leave a row reading only 'not required' without a citation.
checklist.done: every no-action row carries a named basis and a citation.

checklist.step: Compute the six-month Arrangement deadline and back-schedule internal milestones
actions: Take the plan-year effective date and subtract six months to get the FEMA return deadline.
Back-schedule internal milestones: legal review of the Arrangement (T-8 months), signature routing (T-7 months), FEMA submission (T-6.5 months).
Load milestones into Internal Regulatory System and set T-9/T-7/T-6 month reminders.
checklist.done: the FEMA return deadline and internal milestones are computed and loaded with reminders.

checklist.step: Confirm the Elevation Certificate form version in use is current
actions: Check the FEMA Elevation Certificate (Form FF-206-FY-22-152) expiration/renewal date on FEMA's forms page.
Compare to the version embedded in underwriting workstation templates and rating worksheets.
Flag a mismatch for the Policy Administration Analyst to correct before the next rating cycle.
checklist.done: the Elevation Certificate version in active use matches the current FEMA-published form.

checklist.step: Write the determination log entry for the FY cycle
actions: For every worksheet row, add a log entry: FY, item, tag, action required Y/N, citation, accountable performer, target date, decider and decision date.
Link each entry to the determination folder holding the Federal Register capture and the Manual redline.
Set status to 'Determined — pending counsel' for every ARRANGEMENT or STATE-INFORMATIONAL row, else 'Determined — closed'.
checklist.done: the log holds one complete, source-linked entry per item with no blank fields.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel sign-off on the Arrangement redline and any no-action call
actions: Route the Arrangement redline and every NON-FILED row to counsel.
Counsel confirms the Arrangement can be signed unmodified, or flags any clause requiring a company-specific side letter request to FEMA.
Counsel confirms or overturns each no-action basis in writing on the worksheet.
Overturned rows return to the Product Filing Specialist for rework within the same week.
checklist.done: no ARRANGEMENT or no-action row is closed without a dated counsel confirmation.

checklist.step: Publish the determination to Product Compliance leadership and arm the FEMA-return gate
actions: Attach the determination summary to the annual WYO onboarding record.
Set a hard gate: no new plan-year SFIP business may be bound until the executed Arrangement is confirmed submitted and, where required, TRRP re-certification confirmed live.
Distribute the milestone calendar to Regulatory Filing Specialist, Policy Administration Analyst and Insurance Product Manager.
checklist.done: the determination is published and the FEMA-return gate is set with a shared milestone calendar.

checklist.step: Escalate when the six-month window cannot be met
actions: Compare today's date plus the legal-review and signature-routing lead time to the FEMA six-month deadline.
Where the deadline is already unreachable, escalate to Head of Compliance and General Counsel within one business day.
Present options in writing: expedited signature routing, a request to FEMA/NFIP BSA for guidance, or a hold on new NFIP business in the affected plan year.
Record the decision and owner on the determination log — silently missing the deadline is never an option.
checklist.done: every at-risk deadline has a written, owned decision on the log.

checklist.step: Retain the FY determination package
actions: Move the determination folder (worksheet, Federal Register capture, Manual redline, counsel sign-offs) into the compliance evidence repository under the FEMA fiscal year.
Apply the 5-year retention label consistent with FEMA OIG audit look-back.
Confirm the repository index shows the record searchable by FY and Arrangement citation.
checklist.done: the FY determination package is filed, labelled for 5-year retention, and retrievable by fiscal year.

testing.step: Build the population of FY determination cycles and mid-year bulletins
actions: Extract from Internal Regulatory System every FEMA fiscal-year Arrangement cycle and every mid-year Flood Insurance Manual or form bulletin logged in the test period.
Reconcile the extract count to the Federal Register tracking log for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before drawing the sample.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the Federal Register tracking log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every cycle to a completed, signed-off determination
actions: Match each population row to a determination log entry.
Check the determination decision date precedes the FEMA six-month deadline for that FY.
List unmatched or late rows as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a timely determination or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Arrangement re-subscription cycles in the test period.
Take a random sample of at least 10 of the remaining state-informational and system-only rows.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every Arrangement cycle.

testing.step: Re-perform the Federal Register read for each sampled Arrangement cycle
actions: Pull the Federal Register notice for the sampled FY independently and read the Arrangement's effective date and any conditions.
Independently compute the six-month deadline and compare to the logged determination.
Any difference, including a right conclusion reached on a stale citation, is an exception.
Capture the Federal Register page into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled cycle has an independently re-performed deadline calculation and a captured source page.

testing.step: Test community participation checks on the sample
actions: For sampled communities, independently query FEMA's Community Status Book / Community Information System as of the determination date.
Compare the status found to the status recorded on the worksheet.
Flag any community that was suspended or probationary but was not escalated.
testing.done: recorded community status matches an independent Community Status Book check, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify counsel sign-off exists and pre-dates the FEMA submission
actions: Pull each sampled ARRANGEMENT row and confirm a dated counsel sign-off exists.
Confirm the sign-off date pre-dates the Arrangement submission date to FEMA.
Treat a missing or undated sign-off as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled Arrangement row carries a dated, pre-submission counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Trace the Elevation Certificate version check on the sample
actions: For sampled cycles, confirm the FEMA Elevation Certificate form version noted matches FEMA's currently published form.
Trace the version check to the underwriting workstation template in use during the cycle.
Flag any cycle where a stale form version was in active use.
testing.done: the Elevation Certificate version check is independently confirmed for each sampled cycle.

testing.step: Recompute the six-month milestone schedule
actions: For 5 sampled cycles, recompute the milestone back-schedule (legal review, signature routing, FEMA submission) from the plan-year effective date.
Compare recomputed milestones to what was actually loaded into Internal Regulatory System.
Any milestone that was set after its recomputed date is a reportable timing gap.
testing.done: recomputed milestones reconcile to the loaded calendar for every sampled cycle.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the FY, the item, and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (missed Federal Register alert, stale Manual version, uncaptured community suspension) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into next cycle's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for the Arrangement deadline.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared none of the sampled determinations, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any open community-suspension findings to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns assembly of the WYO filing package — the executed Arrangement signature set, the TRRP test/certification tapes, and the monthly WYO Financial Control Plan statements and reconciliations — before submission to FEMA/NFIP BSA.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 44 CFR 62.24(c) (WYO participation criteria) and the current WYO Financial Control Plan, re-read each time TRRP re-certification or a new plan-year package is assembled

In-scope processes.value: WYO package assembly — from a confirmed determination that TRRP re-certification or a plan-year package is required, through zero-error test-tape submission, monthly financial statement preparation, and reconciliation sign-off

In-scope systems.value: Policy Administration Platform generates the monthly policy/claims transaction extract fed into the TRRP test and production tapes; Microsoft Excel builds the Financial Control Plan reconciliation workpapers

Compliance procedure documented.value: WYO Package Preparation Procedure — TRRP test-tape build, zero-error validation, Financial Control Plan monthly statement build, reconciliation to the general ledger, and package assembly

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Controller and Head of Compliance jointly; reviewed annually and on any NFIP BSA layout change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: TRRP test tapes must pass with zero errors before onboarding is confirmed; production monthly output tapes and Financial Control Plan statements are due to NFIP BSA on the monthly cycle date set in the WYO calendar

Deadline reminders configured.value: Policy Administration Platform close calendar flags the monthly extract-build date 5 business days ahead of the NFIP BSA submission date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Test-tape validation logs, monthly output tapes, Financial Control Plan statements and reconciliations retained 5 years, consistent with FEMA OIG/NFIP BSA audit look-back

checklist.step: Confirm package scope from the determination log
actions: Pull the current-cycle determination log rows tagged ARRANGEMENT and TRRP.
Confirm with the Regulatory Reporting Analyst whether this is a first-time TRRP certification, a re-certification, or a routine monthly production cycle.
Open a package folder named <FY>-WYO-package and attach the determination rows.
checklist.done: the package folder is open with the determination rows confirming what must be assembled.

checklist.step: Build the policy and claims transaction extract
actions: In Policy Administration Platform, run the monthly TRRP extract job covering all in-force, new, endorsed, cancelled and claim transactions in the period.
Confirm the extract covers every writing company/co-code and every SFIP form type (Dwelling, General Property, RCBAP, Homeowner Flood Form).
Export to the TRRP Plan D layout and stage the file in the package folder.
checklist.done: a staged TRRP-layout extract exists covering every form type and writing company for the period.

checklist.step: Run the zero-error validation on the test tape
actions: Run the TRRP pre-submission validator against the staged extract.
Review every flagged record: missing community number, invalid Elevation Certificate reference, out-of-range premium/loss field.
Correct source data in Policy Administration Platform and re-run the extract until the validator returns zero errors.
Save the final zero-error validation log.
checklist.done: the validation log shows zero errors on the final extract run.

checklist.step: Prepare the Financial Control Plan monthly statement
actions: Populate the Financial Control Plan statement template with written premium, ceded-to-FEMA premium, incurred losses and ULAE/ALAE per WYO Arrangement Art. III.C.
Pull comparison totals from the general ledger for the same period.
Flag any line item lacking a general-ledger source as incomplete.
checklist.done: the Financial Control Plan statement is populated with every line sourced to the general ledger.

checklist.step: Reconcile the statement to the general ledger
actions: Pull the flood line-of-business trial balance for the period from the general ledger.
Compare each Financial Control Plan line to its general-ledger counterpart and document every variance.
Resolve variances above a zero-tolerance threshold before the statement is finalized; log unresolved items as exceptions.
checklist.done: every Financial Control Plan line reconciles to the general ledger or carries a logged, owned exception.

checklist.step: Compile the Arrangement signature package
actions: Assemble the executed-copy signature page, corporate authority documentation, and the unmodified Arrangement text for signature routing.
Confirm no clause was altered from the Federal Register-published text.
Route for internal signature per the delegation of authority matrix.
checklist.done: the signature package is assembled unmodified and routed for internal signature.

checklist.step: Prepare state informational filing drafts where required
actions: For each state flagged in the determination log, draft the SERFF informational filing referencing the current SFIP/Homeowner Flood Form edition and Manual rating basis.
Attach the current form PDFs with edition dates and the FEMA Manual transmittal page as supporting documentation.
Complete the SERFF transmittal fields (TOI: Fire/Allied Lines — Flood, filing type: Informational).
checklist.done: a SERFF-ready informational filing draft exists for every flagged state, with forms and transmittal attached.

checklist.step: Have the Product / Filing Actuary review the reconciliation memo
actions: Read the Financial Control Plan reconciliation memo for consistency with the NFIP Flood Insurance Manual rating basis in force for the period.
Confirm ULAE/ALAE figures follow the WYO Arrangement Art. III.C reimbursement formula.
Sign the memo or return it with dated comments.
checklist.done: the reconciliation memo carries a dated actuarial sign-off or documented comments resolved.

checklist.step: Assemble the full package and run a completeness check
actions: Checklist the package against the determination log: Arrangement signature set, TRRP zero-error tape, Financial Control Plan statement, reconciliation memo, and state informational drafts.
Confirm every attachment carries the correct file naming convention and version date.
Flag any missing item and chase the accountable performer before proceeding.
checklist.done: the completeness check shows every determined item present and correctly named.

checklist.step: Route the package for internal review
actions: Circulate the assembled package to Controller, Product / Filing Actuary and Regulatory Counsel for parallel review.
Log each reviewer's sign-off date and any comments.
Do not release the package to submission until all three sign-offs are recorded.
checklist.done: Controller, Actuary and Regulatory Counsel sign-offs are all recorded on the package.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel sign-off on the Arrangement package specifically
actions: Confirm the Arrangement text is unmodified from the Federal Register publication.
Confirm corporate signature authority matches the delegation of authority matrix.
Sign the package cover sheet or return it with required corrections.
checklist.done: counsel has signed the Arrangement package cover sheet confirming text and authority are correct.

checklist.step: Stage the package for submission with a target date
actions: Set the package status to 'Ready for submission' in Internal Regulatory System.
Confirm the staged submission date leaves the FEMA six-month Arrangement window and the monthly TRRP cycle date intact.
Hand off to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for submission and tracking.
checklist.done: the package is staged 'Ready for submission' with a target date inside every applicable deadline.

checklist.step: Escalate any package component that cannot be completed on time
actions: Identify any component (validation errors unresolved, reconciliation break open, missing sign-off) at risk of missing the submission date.
Escalate to Head of Compliance within one business day of identification.
Record the decision (extend internal deadline, escalate to FEMA/NFIP BSA for guidance, or partial submission with a documented gap) on the package record.
checklist.done: every at-risk component has a written, owned decision before the submission date.

checklist.step: Version and archive the assembled package
actions: Save the final package version with a version number and date into the compliance evidence repository.
Lock the version so subsequent edits create a new version rather than overwriting.
Confirm the repository entry links back to the determination log row it fulfills.
checklist.done: the final package is versioned, locked and linked to its determination log row.

checklist.step: Confirm the extract and package tie to the prior month's closing balances
actions: Compare the period's opening in-force policy count and premium to the prior period's closing figures.
Investigate and document any unexplained jump or drop before the package is finalized.
Attach the roll-forward reconciliation to the package folder.
checklist.done: the roll-forward from the prior period's closing balances is documented and attached.

testing.step: Build the population of monthly TRRP/Financial Control Plan packages
actions: Extract from Internal Regulatory System every package staged 'Ready for submission' or later in the test period.
Reconcile the count to the Policy Administration Platform extract job log for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the extract job log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every package to a zero-error validation log
actions: Match each population row to its final TRRP validation log.
Confirm the log shows zero errors on the version actually submitted, not an earlier failed run.
List any package submitted without a zero-error log as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a zero-error validation log for the submitted version.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 3 full months at random (seeded, reproducible) plus any month flagged with a reconciliation break.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and includes every flagged reconciliation-break month.

testing.step: Re-perform the reconciliation to the general ledger
actions: Independently pull the flood line-of-business trial balance for each sampled month.
Recompute each Financial Control Plan line against the trial balance without referencing the prepared reconciliation first.
Compare to the recorded reconciliation; any variance not already logged as an exception is a new finding.
testing.done: each sampled month has an independent reconciliation re-performance with variances compared to what was logged.

testing.step: Re-run the TRRP validator on a sampled extract
actions: Pull the raw Policy Administration Platform extract underlying two sampled months before any correction was applied.
Run the TRRP validator independently and compare error counts to what the Regulatory Reporting Analyst reported.
Confirm the final zero-error tape matches what was actually submitted to NFIP BSA.
testing.done: the independently re-run validator result matches the reported error count and the submitted tape.

testing.step: Verify the ULAE/ALAE reimbursement calculation
actions: For each sampled month, recompute ULAE/ALAE reimbursement per the WYO Arrangement Art. III.C formula.
Compare to the figure submitted in the Financial Control Plan statement.
Flag any variance for Controller review.
testing.done: recomputed ULAE/ALAE reconciles to the submitted figure for every sampled month, or a flagged variance is on record.

testing.step: Trace the state informational filings to SERFF disposition
actions: For each sampled state informational filing, open SERFF Filing Access and confirm the submission exists and matches the attached forms.
Confirm the filing carries the correct TOI and form edition dates.
Capture the SERFF filing summary screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state informational filing is traced to a matching, correctly coded SERFF submission.

testing.step: Test the completeness check evidence on the sample
actions: For each sampled package, confirm the completeness checklist was actually completed and dated before submission staging.
Confirm all three required internal sign-offs (Controller, Actuary, Regulatory Counsel) are present and dated before the submission date.
Flag any package submitted before all sign-offs were recorded.
testing.done: every sampled package shows a completed checklist and three pre-submission sign-offs, or a flagged gap.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the month, the component that failed, and the reporting impact.
Assign a root cause (source data defect, layout change missed, late sign-off) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next month's package build as a mandatory check.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and next-cycle check.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare to the zero-error / zero-variance thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared none of the sampled packages, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Confirm the package or filing is release-ready
actions: Pull the package or state informational filing draft staged 'Ready for submission'.
Confirm all required sign-offs (Controller, Actuary, Regulatory Counsel) are present and dated.
Reject anything missing a sign-off back to Product Filing Specialist rather than submitting around it.
checklist.done: only sign-off-complete packages proceed to submission.

checklist.step: Submit the Arrangement and TRRP package to FEMA/NFIP BSA
actions: Transmit the executed Arrangement and the zero-error TRRP output tape through the designated NFIP BSA submission channel.
Log the submission date, method and confirmation number in Internal Regulatory System.
Set the tracking status to 'Submitted — awaiting acknowledgment'.
checklist.done: the FEMA/NFIP BSA submission is logged with a date, method and confirmation reference.

checklist.step: Submit each state informational filing via SERFF
actions: In SERFF, open the drafted informational filing for the state and confirm all transmittal fields (TOI, form edition dates, filing type) are complete.
Submit the filing and record the SERFF Tracking Number and submission date.
Repeat for every state flagged in the determination log.
checklist.done: every flagged state's informational filing is submitted with a SERFF Tracking Number on record.

checklist.step: Confirm receipt on both channels
actions: Check SERFF Filing Access for a status change from 'Submitted' to 'In Review'.
Check Internal Regulatory System correspondence log for a FEMA/NFIP BSA receipt confirmation.
Where no receipt appears within 5 business days, follow up with the submission channel's support contact and log the follow-up.
checklist.done: receipt is confirmed on both channels, or a documented follow-up is on record for any silent submission.

checklist.step: Monitor SERFF for objections or requests for additional information
actions: Check SERFF Filing Access daily for status changes on open state filings.
Open any objection or request for additional information and log the state's stated response deadline.
Route the objection to the Product Filing Specialist and Regulatory Counsel the same day it appears.
checklist.done: every SERFF status change is checked and any objection is routed the same day.

checklist.step: Monitor FEMA/NFIP BSA correspondence for acknowledgment or a query
actions: Check the designated FEMA/NFIP BSA correspondence channel for an acknowledgment letter or a data query on the submitted tape/statement.
Log any query with its stated response deadline in Internal Regulatory System.
Route data queries to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst for same-week resolution.
checklist.done: FEMA/NFIP BSA correspondence is checked and any query is logged with its deadline and routed.

checklist.step: Track each SERFF filing to a closed disposition
actions: Update the tracking log each time a SERFF filing's disposition changes.
On a Filed/Approved/Closed-Approved disposition, capture the disposition date and screenshot into the record.
On an adverse disposition (Disapproved/Closed-Withdrawn), escalate immediately to Compliance Officer and Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: every SERFF filing shows a captured, dated final disposition, with adverse outcomes escalated same-day.

checklist.step: Track the FEMA/NFIP BSA submission to closed acknowledgment
actions: Confirm FEMA/NFIP BSA's final acknowledgment letter or reconciliation-accepted notice is received.
File the acknowledgment against the submission record in Internal Regulatory System.
Set tracking status to 'Closed — acknowledged'.
checklist.done: every FEMA/NFIP BSA submission carries a filed acknowledgment and a closed tracking status.

checklist.step: Reconcile the disposition log to the determination log weekly
actions: Compare open items on the disposition log to the corresponding determination log rows.
Confirm no determined item has been sitting open past its expected acknowledgment window without a follow-up.
Report the week's open-item count to the Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: the weekly reconciliation shows no unexplained open item and a reported count.

checklist.step: Notify Insurance Product Manager the moment a gating item closes
actions: The instant an Arrangement, TRRP or state informational filing closes favorably, notify the Insurance Product Manager by name.
Include the disposition date and reference number in the notification.
Update the release-gate record referenced in the hold-release control.
checklist.done: the Insurance Product Manager is notified same-day of every favorable closure with the disposition reference.

checklist.step: Escalate stalled submissions
actions: Identify any submission open beyond its expected acknowledgment window (15/30/45-day thresholds).
Escalate to Compliance Officer with the submission history and follow-ups already attempted.
Record the escalation outcome and any revised expected closure date on the tracking log.
checklist.done: every stalled submission is escalated with a documented follow-up history and a revised expected date.

checklist.step: Clear objections and interrogatories that arrive on a submission
actions: Draft the response using the source documentation already in the package folder.
Route the draft through Product / Filing Actuary or Regulatory Counsel as the subject matter requires.
Submit the response through the same channel (SERFF or FEMA/NFIP BSA correspondence) before the stated deadline and log the submission.
checklist.done: every objection response is submitted before its deadline through the same channel it arrived on, and logged.

checklist.step: Verify the final approved/filed text matches what implementation will use
actions: Compare the SERFF-approved form/rate text (if amended during review) to the version staged for system implementation.
Flag any discrepancy to the Policy Administration Analyst before implementation begins.
Confirm the final approved version is the one saved to the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the version staged for implementation matches the final approved/filed text with no discrepancy.

checklist.step: Close out the tracking record and hand off for retention
actions: Set the tracking record to 'Closed' once every gating item shows a favorable, dated disposition.
Compile the disposition evidence set (SERFF screens, FEMA/NFIP BSA acknowledgment) for hand-off.
Notify Compliance Ops the record is ready for retention filing.
checklist.done: the tracking record is closed and the disposition evidence set is handed off for retention.

checklist.step: Report monthly submission status to Product Compliance leadership
actions: Compile a monthly status report: submissions made, closed favorably, open, and any adverse disposition.
Circulate to Head of Compliance and Insurance Product Manager.
Retain the report alongside the month's tracking log.
checklist.done: a monthly status report is compiled, circulated and retained.

testing.step: Build the population of submissions made in the period
actions: Extract every SERFF submission from Filing Access and every FEMA/NFIP BSA submission from Internal Regulatory System for the test period.
Reconcile the combined count to the monthly status reports issued in the period.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the monthly status reports and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every submission to a logged disposition
actions: Match each population row to a tracking-log disposition entry.
Check the disposition date is present and the status is either closed favorably or has an active, documented follow-up.
List unmatched or undocumented rows as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a disposition entry or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of adverse or still-open dispositions at test date.
Take a random sample of at least 15 closed-favorable rows.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every adverse or open disposition.

testing.step: Trace each sampled SERFF row to the live disposition
actions: Open SERFF Filing Access and search the SERFF Tracking Number for each sampled row.
Confirm the live disposition matches what is logged, including the disposition date.
Screenshot the SERFF disposition screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled SERFF row's live disposition matches the log, with a captured screen.

testing.step: Confirm FEMA/NFIP BSA acknowledgment letters exist for the sample
actions: For each sampled FEMA/NFIP BSA row, locate the filed acknowledgment correspondence in Internal Regulatory System.
Confirm the acknowledgment references the correct submission (Arrangement, TRRP tape or Financial Control Plan statement) and date.
Flag any row lacking a filed acknowledgment as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled FEMA/NFIP BSA row has a filed, matching acknowledgment or a logged exception.

testing.step: Recompute the follow-up timeliness on open items
actions: For every sampled item still open, compute days elapsed since submission against the 15/30/45-day thresholds.
Compare to the follow-up dates actually logged.
Flag any item that passed a threshold without a logged follow-up.
testing.done: follow-up timeliness is recomputed for every open sampled item and compared to the log.

testing.step: Test the objection-response evidence on the sample
actions: For sampled rows with a logged objection, pull the response and confirm it was submitted through the same channel it arrived on.
Confirm the response was submitted before the state or FEMA/NFIP BSA deadline.
Flag any late or channel-mismatched response.
testing.done: every sampled objection response is confirmed timely and channel-correct, or flagged.

testing.step: Verify the escalation trail on adverse dispositions
actions: For every adverse disposition in the population, confirm same-day escalation to Compliance Officer and Regulatory Counsel is documented.
Confirm a written remediation decision exists on the tracking record.
Flag any adverse disposition lacking a documented, timely escalation.
testing.done: every adverse disposition shows a documented same-day escalation and a written remediation decision.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the submission id, channel, and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (missed follow-up threshold, stale evidence, wrong channel) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into next month's tracking as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare to the closed-favorable-disposition threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who tracked none of the sampled submissions, sign the workpaper.
Report results and any adverse dispositions to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the release gate — no new-business SFIP may be bound in any state or community until the Arrangement is confirmed executed for the plan year, TRRP certification is live, community participation is confirmed current, and any state informational filing is closed.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 44 CFR 62.24(c) (WYO participation criteria) and 44 CFR Part 59/60 (community eligibility), checked against the release gate record before every gate is lifted

In-scope processes.value: Product release gating — from a closed favorable disposition on every gating item through the formal lift of the new-business hold in Policy Administration Platform

In-scope systems.value: Policy Administration Platform carries the system-level new-business block by state/community; Internal Regulatory System is the source of truth for whether the gating conditions are met

Compliance procedure documented.value: WYO Release Gate Procedure — gating condition checklist, system block configuration, gate-lift approval, and post-lift verification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance and Chief Underwriting Officer jointly; reviewed each plan year

Deadline reminders configured.value: Internal Regulatory System alerts Insurance Product Manager the moment every gating item on the disposition log shows a favorable, closed status

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Release gate record, gating condition evidence, and gate-lift approval retained 5 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any new-business bind found to have occurred before the gate was lifted is logged as an exception and reported as a potential unauthorized-writing breach

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Compliance Officer signs off the remediation plan for any premature bind, including any required self-report to FEMA

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every new-business SFIP bound in the test period, drawn from Policy Administration Platform, cross-referenced to the release gate record for that state/community

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Continuous system control tested monthly over the period's new-business population

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly release-gate test workpaper filed in the compliance evidence repository

checklist.step: Set the default new-business gate closed for every plan year
actions: At the start of each plan-year determination cycle, set the default new-business SFIP bind flag to blocked for every state/community pending confirmation.
Confirm with the Policy Administration Analyst that the block is enforced at the rating/quote step, not only at issuance.
Log the default-closed status in the release gate record.
checklist.done: the release gate record shows every state/community defaulted to blocked pending confirmation.

checklist.step: Define the gating conditions per state/community
actions: List, per state, the required conditions: Arrangement executed and acknowledged, TRRP certification live, and (where flagged) state informational filing closed.
List, per community, the required condition: current participating status in FEMA's Community Status Book.
Attach the condition list to the release gate record.
checklist.done: every state and community carries an explicit, attached list of gating conditions.

checklist.step: Monitor the disposition log for gating conditions closing
actions: Check the disposition log daily during an active gating cycle for status changes on Arrangement, TRRP or state informational items.
Cross-reference each closure to the specific state/community it satisfies.
Update the release gate record the same day a condition closes.
checklist.done: the release gate record is updated same-day as each gating condition closes.

checklist.step: Independently reconfirm community participation status before lifting a community gate
actions: Query FEMA's Community Status Book / Community Information System for the community as of the day the gate is to be lifted.
Confirm participating, non-suspended status.
Log the query date and result on the release gate record before proceeding.
checklist.done: a same-day community status query result is logged before any community gate is lifted.

checklist.step: Confirm every condition is met before drafting a gate-lift request
actions: Checklist all required conditions for the state/community against the disposition log.
Confirm no condition shows 'Submitted — awaiting acknowledgment' or 'Open'.
Draft the gate-lift request only once every condition shows a favorable, closed status.
checklist.done: the gate-lift request is drafted only after every listed condition shows closed and favorable.

checklist.step: Route the gate-lift request for approval
actions: Attach the disposition evidence (Arrangement acknowledgment, TRRP certification confirmation, community status query, SERFF disposition) to the request.
Route to Chief Underwriting Officer and Head of Compliance for approval.
Log the approval date and approver names on the release gate record.
checklist.done: the gate-lift request carries attached evidence and two named, dated approvals.

checklist.step: Lift the system block in Policy Administration Platform
actions: In Policy Administration Platform, open the new-business rating configuration for the state/community and remove the bind block only for that scope.
Confirm the block remains in place for every other unapproved state/community.
Log the system change ticket number against the release gate record.
checklist.done: the system block is removed only for the approved scope, with every other scope still blocked, and a change ticket logged.

checklist.step: Verify the lift in a test quote before announcing availability
actions: Run a test new-business quote for the approved state/community and confirm it proceeds to bind without a system block.
Run a test quote for a still-blocked state/community and confirm the block still fires.
Attach both test results to the release gate record.
checklist.done: test quotes confirm the lift applied to the approved scope only, with results attached.

checklist.step: Notify Distribution and underwriting of the lifted gate
actions: Notify Underwriting Director / Manager and Broker Relationship Manager by name that new-business flood binding is available for the state/community effective the lift date.
Include the effective date and any conditions on binding (e.g., forms in use, Manual edition).
File the notification against the release gate record.
checklist.done: Underwriting and Distribution leads are notified by name with the effective date and conditions.

checklist.step: Reject and reverse any premature bind found
actions: If a new-business SFIP is found bound in a state/community whose gate had not yet lifted, immediately flag it in Policy Administration Platform.
Notify Insurance Product Manager and Compliance Officer the same day.
Do not cancel unilaterally — hold for Compliance Officer's remediation instruction.
checklist.done: any premature bind found is flagged same-day and held for Compliance Officer instruction, never quietly reversed.

checklist.step: Escalate a premature bind for potential FEMA self-report
actions: Assess whether the premature bind constitutes writing outside an executed Arrangement or in a suspended community.
Route to Regulatory Counsel for a self-report determination to FEMA/NFIP BSA.
Record the determination and any self-report filed on the exception record.
checklist.done: every premature bind carries a documented self-report determination and, where required, a filed self-report.

checklist.step: Re-close the gate immediately if a condition lapses
actions: If a community's status changes to suspended or probationary, or the Arrangement is found deficient, re-apply the system block within the same business day.
Notify Underwriting Director / Manager the block is back in effect and why.
Log the re-closure date and reason on the release gate record.
checklist.done: any lapsed condition triggers a same-day re-block, notification and logged reason.

checklist.step: Reconcile the release gate record to the disposition log monthly
actions: Compare every open or lifted gate on the release gate record to the current disposition log status.
Flag any gate showing lifted in the system but not supported by a closed disposition.
Report the reconciliation result to Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: the monthly reconciliation shows every lifted gate supported by a closed disposition, with results reported.

checklist.step: Retain the gate-lift evidence set
actions: File the gate-lift request, evidence attachments, approvals and test quote results in the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 5-year retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by state/community and plan year.
checklist.done: the gate-lift evidence set is filed, labelled and retrievable by state/community.

checklist.step: Report gate status to the Compliance Committee each cycle
actions: Compile the current status of every state/community gate (blocked, lifted, re-closed) each plan-year cycle.
Present to the Compliance Committee with any premature-bind findings and self-reports.
File the presentation with the cycle's release gate records.
checklist.done: gate status is reported to the Compliance Committee each cycle and filed.

testing.step: Build the population of new-business SFIP binds in the period
actions: Extract every new-business SFIP bind in the test period from Policy Administration Platform, by state and community number.
Reconcile the extract count to the underwriting bind report for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the underwriting bind report and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every bind to a lifted gate that pre-dates it
actions: Match each bind's state/community and date to the release gate record.
Confirm the gate-lift date is earlier than the bind date.
List unmatched or bind-before-lift rows as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every bind is matched to a pre-dated gate lift or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of binds in any state/community that had a gate lifted during the test period.
Take a random sample of at least 25 binds from states/communities gated before the period began.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every newly-lifted gate.

testing.step: Independently re-verify the gating conditions for sampled lifts
actions: For each sampled gate lift, independently pull the disposition log status as of the lift date for Arrangement, TRRP and any state informational filing.
Confirm each condition was actually closed favorably before the lift date, not merely submitted.
Any condition not truly closed before the lift is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled gate lift's conditions are independently confirmed closed before the lift date.

testing.step: Independently re-query community participation status
actions: For sampled community-gated binds, independently query FEMA's Community Status Book as of the bind date.
Compare to the status logged on the release gate record.
Flag any community that was suspended or probationary at bind date.
testing.done: community status at bind date is independently confirmed for every sampled row, with any suspension flagged.

testing.step: Test the two-named-approval control on sampled gate lifts
actions: Confirm each sampled gate lift carries dated approvals from both Chief Underwriting Officer and Head of Compliance.
Confirm the approval dates precede the system-block-removal ticket date.
Flag any lift missing one of the two required approvals.
testing.done: every sampled gate lift shows both required, pre-dated approvals or a flagged gap.

testing.step: Re-perform the test-quote verification
actions: For 5 sampled lifts, independently run a test quote in the approved state/community and a still-blocked comparison state/community.
Confirm the approved scope proceeds and the unapproved scope still blocks.
Any scope leakage (block missing where it should exist, or present where it should not) is a reportable control failure.
testing.done: independent test quotes confirm scope-correct blocking for every sampled lift.

testing.step: Verify the escalation trail on any premature bind identified
actions: For any premature bind found in the population reconciliation, confirm same-day flagging, Compliance Officer notification, and a documented self-report determination.
Confirm no unilateral cancellation occurred outside the documented remediation instruction.
Flag any premature bind lacking a full escalation trail.
testing.done: every premature bind shows a documented, same-day escalation and remediation trail.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the state/community, the bind date, and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (block not configured, condition marked closed prematurely, community status not re-checked) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance premature-bind threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who configured or approved none of the sampled gates, sign the workpaper.
Report results and any self-reports to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 44 CFR 62.23(h)(2) (rate and rule conformance) and the current NFIP Flood Insurance Manual transmittal, re-read at every Manual edition change (typically effective April 1)

In-scope processes.value: Rating/forms system implementation — from a confirmed Manual edition change through configuration, UAT and production release in the policy admin and rating engine, covering every SFIP form type (Dwelling, General Property, RCBAP, Homeowner Flood Form)

In-scope systems.value: Guidewire PolicyCenter carries the flood rating tables, underwriting rules and form templates; changes are built and released through the standard IT change pipeline

Compliance procedure documented.value: NFIP Manual Implementation Procedure — change intake from the Manual transmittal, configuration build, parallel-rate testing against FEMA's published tables, UAT sign-off, and production release timed to the Manual's effective date

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Chief Underwriting Officer and Head of IT jointly; reviewed at each annual Manual edition and any mid-year bulletin

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Production release must be live no later than the Manual's stated effective date (commonly April 1); rating on the prior edition after that date is a compliance breach

Deadline reminders configured.value: IT change calendar milestone alerts at T-60/T-30/T-10 days against the Manual effective date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All NFIP rating table, underwriting rule and form template configuration items released in the test period, drawn from the IT change log

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Test runs at every Manual edition release, supplemented by a quarterly spot-check of live rating output against the current Manual

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built or deployed the configuration being tested

checklist.step: Intake the new Manual edition or bulletin as a system change request
actions: Pull the Manual redline and change list logged by Product Filing Specialist in the annual determination.
Open an IT change request per affected module (rating engine, form templates, underwriting rules) referencing the Manual transmittal page.
Attach the FEMA-published transmittal PDF to each change request.
checklist.done: an IT change request exists per affected module, linked to the Manual transmittal.

checklist.step: Map every changed rating factor to its configuration location
actions: In PolicyCenter, locate the rating table, factor, or rule matching each changed Manual page.
Record the table/field name and current value next to the new Manual value on the mapping worksheet.
Flag any Manual change with no obvious PolicyCenter equivalent for Business Systems Analyst review.
checklist.done: every changed Manual item is mapped to a named PolicyCenter table/field with old and new values recorded.

checklist.step: Build the configuration change in a non-production environment
actions: Apply the mapped rating table, rule and form template changes in the UAT environment.
Enter the new Manual values exactly as published, with no rounding or company adjustment.
Version the configuration change with the Manual edition identifier.
checklist.done: the configuration change is built in UAT, versioned to the Manual edition.

checklist.step: Load the current SFIP form editions into the form template library
actions: Pull the current Dwelling Form, General Property Form, RCBAP and Homeowner Flood Form PDFs with their edition dates.
Load each into the PolicyCenter form template library, replacing the prior edition and preserving the prior edition as an archived version.
Confirm the standalone-issuance rule (44 CFR 62.23(i)(1)) is enforced — no flood form can be selected as an endorsement to a non-flood policy.
checklist.done: current form editions are loaded, prior editions archived, and the standalone-issuance rule is confirmed enforced.

checklist.step: Run parallel-rate tests against FEMA's published tables
actions: Select a representative set of test risks spanning zone types (Zone A, AE, V, X, pre-FIRM/post-FIRM) and coverage limits.
Run each test risk through the UAT rating engine and independently calculate the expected premium from the published Manual tables in Microsoft Excel.
Compare system output to the independent calculation line by line and log every variance.
Do not sign off UAT until variances are resolved to zero.
checklist.done: parallel-rate test results show zero variance between system output and independently calculated Manual premiums.

checklist.step: Test the Elevation Certificate data intake against the current form
actions: Confirm the underwriting workstation Elevation Certificate intake fields match FEMA Form FF-206-FY-22-152's current field set.
Enter a sample Elevation Certificate and confirm the rating engine consumes lowest-floor elevation, flood zone and BFE correctly.
Flag any field mismatch to Business Systems Analyst for correction before release.
checklist.done: Elevation Certificate intake fields match the current FEMA form and correctly drive the rating calculation.

checklist.step: Get underwriting sign-off on the rule changes
actions: Review the mapped underwriting rule changes against current underwriting guidelines.
Confirm no company-specific eligibility rule has been layered onto the federally prescribed rules.
Sign the mapping worksheet or return it with corrections.
checklist.done: underwriting has signed the mapping worksheet confirming no non-federal rule was introduced.

checklist.step: Schedule the production release against the Manual effective date
actions: Confirm UAT sign-off and parallel-rate test sign-off are both complete.
Schedule the production deployment date to be live on or before the Manual's stated effective date, with buffer for a rollback window.
Log the scheduled date in the IT change calendar with T-60/T-30/T-10 reminders.
checklist.done: the production release is scheduled on or before the Manual effective date with a logged rollback window.

checklist.step: Deploy to production and verify with a live-environment smoke test
actions: Deploy the change per the standard release pipeline.
Run the same representative test risks used in UAT against production and confirm identical results.
Confirm the effective date on the rating table matches the Manual's stated effective date, not the deployment date, so in-force renewals are not misrated.
checklist.done: production smoke test results match UAT and the rating table's effective date matches the Manual's stated date.

checklist.step: Retire the prior edition from new-business quoting
actions: Confirm the prior Manual edition and prior form editions can no longer be selected for new business or renewal effective on/after the Manual's effective date.
Leave the prior edition accessible for endorsement/audit of policies still in their original term.
Log the retirement date on the release record.
checklist.done: the prior edition is blocked for new business/renewal from the effective date while remaining available for in-term servicing.

checklist.step: Notify Underwriting and Distribution of the go-live
actions: Notify Underwriting Director / Manager and Broker Relationship Manager by name of the go-live date and what changed.
Distribute a summary of rating/rule changes for producer-facing communication.
File the notification against the release record.
checklist.done: Underwriting and Distribution are notified by name with a change summary, filed against the record.

checklist.step: Spot-check live production output in the first cycle after go-live
actions: Pull 10 live new-business quotes bound in the first week after go-live.
Recompute expected premium from the current Manual for each and compare to the bound premium.
Escalate any variance to Business Systems Analyst same-day for a hot-fix.
checklist.done: 10 live post-go-live quotes are spot-checked with zero unresolved variance.

checklist.step: Escalate when a Manual deadline cannot be met
actions: Where testing reveals the release cannot go live by the Manual's effective date, escalate to Chief Underwriting Officer and Compliance Officer within one business day.
Present options in writing: emergency release with reduced testing scope and a documented risk acceptance, or a manual rating workaround with underwriter sign-off for the gap period.
Record the decision and owner — deploying untested is never the default and a rating gap is never silently absorbed.
checklist.done: every at-risk Manual deadline has a written, owned decision before the effective date.

checklist.step: Retain the implementation evidence set
actions: File the mapping worksheet, parallel-rate test results, UAT and underwriting sign-offs, and the release record in the compliance evidence repository under the Manual edition.
Apply the 5-year retention label.
Confirm the record is searchable by Manual edition and effective date.
checklist.done: the implementation evidence set is filed, labelled and retrievable by Manual edition.

checklist.step: Report implementation status to the release gate owner
actions: Notify the Insurance Product Manager once the release is live and spot-checked.
Provide the release date and spot-check result for the release gate record.
File the confirmation against the release record.
checklist.done: the release gate owner is notified with the release date and spot-check result.

testing.step: Build the population of rating/forms configuration releases
actions: Extract every NFIP rating table, rule and form template release from the IT change log in the test period.
Reconcile the extract count to the release calendar for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the release calendar and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every release to a completed parallel-rate test
actions: Match each population row to a parallel-rate test result with zero unresolved variance.
Confirm the test was completed before the production deployment date.
List unmatched or post-deployment-tested rows as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-deployment, zero-variance test or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of annual Manual-edition releases in the test period.
Take a random sample of at least 10 mid-year bulletin releases.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every annual Manual-edition release.

testing.step: Independently recompute premiums against the published Manual
actions: For each sampled release, independently select 5 test risks spanning zone types and coverage limits.
Calculate expected premium from the Manual as published, without referencing the original parallel-rate test.
Run the same test risks through production PolicyCenter and compare.
Any variance is an exception, including ones the original test also missed.
testing.done: independently recomputed premiums match production output for every sampled release, or a variance is logged.

testing.step: Verify form editions in production against FEMA's current publication
actions: For each sampled release, pull the live form template from PolicyCenter and compare its edition date to FEMA's currently published edition.
Confirm no flood form can be selected as an endorsement to a non-flood policy in the live system.
Flag any stale edition or standalone-issuance control gap.
testing.done: form editions in production match FEMA's current publication and the standalone-issuance control is confirmed.

testing.step: Trace the effective-date control on sampled releases
actions: For each sampled release, confirm the rating table's system effective date matches the Manual's stated effective date.
Pull 3 renewals that straddled the effective date and confirm each was rated on the correct edition for its own effective date.
Flag any renewal rated on the wrong edition.
testing.done: the effective-date control is confirmed for every sampled release and straddling renewals rate correctly.

testing.step: Verify underwriting sign-off exists and pre-dates deployment
actions: Confirm each sampled release carries a dated underwriting sign-off on the rule-change mapping.
Confirm the sign-off date precedes the production deployment date.
Flag any release deployed before sign-off.
testing.done: every sampled release shows a pre-deployment underwriting sign-off or a flagged gap.

testing.step: Re-perform the post-go-live spot-check independently
actions: For 2 sampled releases, independently pull 5 live bound quotes from the first week after go-live.
Recompute expected premium and compare to bound premium.
Any variance not already caught and hot-fixed is a new exception.
testing.done: independent post-go-live spot-checks confirm no unresolved variance for the sampled releases.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the Manual edition, the affected rating factor/form, and the compliance and policyholder impact.
Assign a root cause (mapping error, stale form edition, missed effective-date control) and an owner.
Set a remediation date, including any required policyholder premium correction, and carry every open exception into the next release's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where needed, a correction plan.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance rating-variance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who built or deployed none of the sampled releases, sign the workpaper.
Report results and any policyholder-impacting variances to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
